source.method: sparql:SELECT ?item ?itemLabel ?article ?sitelinks ?born WHERE { { SELECT ?item ?sitelinks (GROUP_CONCAT(CONCAT(STR(?bornT), "|", STR(?bornP)); separator=";") AS ?born) WHERE { ?item wdt:P106 wd:Q10873124 ; wikibase:sitelinks ?sitelinks . FILTER(?sitelinks > 30) ?item p:P569 ?bornSt . ?bornSt a wikibase:BestRank . ?bornSt psv:P569 [ wikibase:timeValue ?bornT ; wikibase:timePrecision ?bornP ] . } GROUP BY ?item ?sitelinks ORDER BY DESC(?sitelinks) LIMIT 250 } hint:Prior hint:runFirst true . OPTIONAL { ?article schema:about ?item ; schema:isPartOf <https://en.wikipedia.org/> . } SERVICE wikibase:label { bd:serviceParam wikibase:language "en,mul". } } ORDER BY DESC(?sitelinks) LIMIT 108

born.sort: from the earliest born to the latest

rows.label: Magnus Carlsen
rows.hook: held the top world ranking longer than any other player and won the world championship five times

rows.label: Bobby Fischer
rows.hook: beat a longtime Soviet champion in a world title match that became a Cold War sensation

rows.label: Garry Kasparov
rows.hook: became the youngest world champion of his era and later lost a famous match to a computer program

rows.label: Gukesh D
rows.hook: won the world championship as a teenager, becoming the youngest player ever to hold the title

rows.label: Judit Polgár
rows.hook: is widely considered the strongest woman ever to play the game, beating many top players along the way

rows.label: Hikaru Nakamura
rows.hook: built a massive online following as a top streamer, blitz specialist and commentator

rows.label: Viswanathan Anand
rows.hook: held world titles in classical, rapid and blitz play all at the same time

rows.label: Javokhir Sindarov
rows.description: Uzbek chess grandmaster and 2026 Candidates Tournament winner
rows.hook: won a major candidates tournament as a rising young star, earning a shot at the world title

rows.label: Praggnanandhaa
rows.hook: beat the world's top-ranked player in a rapid event and became one of the youngest grandmasters ever

rows.label: Anatoly Karpov
rows.hook: held the world championship for a decade and was known for a relentless, positional playing style

rows.label: Vladimir Kramnik
rows.hook: ended a legendary champion's long reign at the top in a landmark title match

rows.label: Mikhail Tal
rows.hook: earned a nickname for his dazzling, high-risk attacking style and briefly held the world title

rows.label: Fabiano Caruana
rows.hook: climbed to the top of the world rankings and challenged for the world title in a tiebreak-decided match

rows.label: Wesley So
rows.hook: won a major invitational tournament with a record unbeaten streak and later switched federations

rows.label: Anish Giri
rows.hook: became known for drawing an unusually high share of his games at the top level

rows.label: Ding Liren
rows.description: Chinese grandmaster and former World Chess Champion
rows.hook: became the first world champion from his country, winning the title in a dramatic tiebreak match
